obligations.note: The new compatibility route in app.py's match() returns Route(..., 'view_account_number', mfa=False) for the path /compat/account-number/{id}. The action 'view_account_number' is listed as privileged in controls/payments/access-policy.json, yet this route is dispatched with mfa=False, bypassing the MFA gate in _authenticate. Furthermore, the route is served before the ROUTE_TABLE loop, meaning it is not in the route table, directly violating the clause 'no route is served outside the route table.'

Ticket CHG-26132 is type 'standard', approved by change manager Erik Brandt on 2026-10-15, and its components list includes 'payments.http', which is the component for the sole changed file apps/baseline-payments/payments/app.py per components.json.

A code_review approval exists from mara.costa@fernbrook.example, who is listed in the directory as a change_approver for payments and is not the author (Linh Nguyen, also on payments-eng but only an engineer).
The single commit 265d812… is the head commit, and both approvals (code_review and security_review) name that exact commit, so no later commits could void them.
CI ran on the final commit 265d812… with 172 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped; all registered control tests (including test_privileged_routes_require_mfa) are present, unskipped, and passing.

The changed file app.py belongs to component 'payments.http' which is security_sensitive=true; a security_review approval from kofi.mensah@fernbrook.example (a security_reviewer per the directory) for the same commit is present.

ACR-0404 (MFA-1 evidence) covers apps/baseline-payments/payments/routes.py, which is not modified by this change; the evidence's covered code is unchanged, so the evidence has not lapsed. The MFA-1 violation arises from new code in app.py, not from a lapse of prior evidence.

summary: The change adds a compatibility URL /compat/account-number/{id} in app.py that maps to the privileged action 'view_account_number' but sets mfa=False, and it is dispatched before the route-table loop, meaning it is served outside the route table. This directly violates MFA-1, which requires every route whose action is privileged to demand MFA and forbids any route outside the route table. All process obligations (ticket, independent approval, coverage, CI, security review) are satisfied, but the MFA-1 violation is critical-severity and cannot be waived. The change must be rejected and the compatibility route either placed in the route table with mfa=True or the action declassified with appropriate justification and approval.
